root_idea.summary: The root centers on an allotted share, portion, or lot, especially a share associated with fortune or favorable circumstances.
root_idea.development: The lexical range develops from an apportioned share or lot to good fortune and the state of being fortunate or well-provided.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested noun حَظّ is a standalone lexical headword.

senses.definition: An allotted share, portion, or lot.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic usage, this may denote an assigned portion in an inheritance, a portion of revealed instruction, or a share in a matter or outcome.

senses.definition: Good fortune; a favorable lot or outcome.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of favorable fortune or an advantageous share, including worldly prosperity or a favorable spiritual outcome.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become fortunate, or to possess good fortune.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classical verbal usage, attested with perfect and imperfect forms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become rich, wealthy, or opulent; to be in a state of competence or sufficiency.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived verbal usage describing material abundance or freedom from want.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fortunate; possessing a good share of the means of subsistence; in a reported usage, competent or wealthy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival form describing a person’s favorable condition or adequate provision.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The unit supplies the fortunate verbal sense and the related wealth or sufficiency usage.

cautions: The canonical Quran root حظظ is matched to Lane and Maqayis under the contracted heading حظ.
The Quran-attested form in this packet is the noun حَظّ; the listed verbal and adjectival forms are broader Classical Arabic evidence, not additional Quranic form groups.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: Lane’s preference expression أَحْظَيْتُهُ عَلَيْهِ is materially lexical but its attribution is unresolved: the passage allows derivation from حظظ or from حُظْوَةٌ.
